emergencyNumber: 117 (police), 118 (fire), 191 (ambulance/SAMU). Emergency services are limited — go directly to a hospital if possible.
healthcareSystem: Public healthcare system with very limited resources. CHU Sylvanus Olympio in Lomé is the main hospital. Private clinics in Lomé offer better care. Rural healthcare is extremely basic. French-based medical system.
qualityNotes: Healthcare quality is low by international standards. CHU Sylvanus Olympio in Lomé is the largest facility but faces chronic equipment and supply shortages. Private clinics in Lomé offer better care with shorter wait times. Outside Lomé, medical facilities are very basic. Serious conditions require evacuation to Ghana (Accra) or Europe.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 8am-12:30pm and 3pm-7pm weekdays, Saturday mornings. Duty pharmacies in Lomé for after-hours. Very limited outside the capital.
pharmacyTips: Bring all medications you need from home. Counterfeit drugs are a significant concern — only use established pharmacies (look for the green cross sign). Pharmacies in Lomé carry French medications. Staff speak French. Stock can be unreliable.
prescriptionRules: Prescription medications officially require a doctor's ordonnance, but enforcement is inconsistent. Many medications are sold freely. Bring all needed medications from home as availability is unreliable and counterfeit drugs are common.

restrictedMeds.name: Controlled narcotics
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter and original prescription. Keep medications in original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Requires documentation for import. Carry prescriptions and a doctor's letter.

bringDocumentation: Bring prescriptions (French translations ideal), a doctor's letter listing all medications, yellow fever vaccination certificate (required), travel insurance documentation, and copies of all important medical records.

travelInsurance.tips: Essential for travel to Togo. Ensure coverage includes medical evacuation to Accra (Ghana), South Africa, or Europe. Local facilities cannot handle serious conditions. Cash payment is the norm at all facilities.

recommended: Routine vaccinations (MMR, diphtheria-tetanus-pertussis, varicella, polio, flu)
vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever vaccination is REQUIRED for all travelers. Malaria is widespread — take prophylaxis, sleep under insecticide-treated mosquito nets, and use repellent. Consult a travel medicine clinic 4-6 weeks before departure.

waterNotes: Tap water is NOT safe to drink anywhere in Togo. Use only bottled or purified water for drinking, brushing teeth, and making ice. Boil water if bottled water is unavailable. Avoid ice in drinks unless confirmed purified.
foodSafetyTips: Eat only thoroughly cooked food served hot. Avoid raw vegetables, salads, and unpeeled fruits unless you wash and peel them yourself. Street food is popular but carries higher risk. Stick to busy vendors where food turnover is high. Wash hands frequently.
medicalTourismNote: Togo is not a medical tourism destination. Patients requiring advanced care are evacuated to Accra (Ghana), Abidjan (Côte d'Ivoire), or European cities.
sources: French Ministry of Foreign Affairs Travel Advisory

hospitals.name: CHU Sylvanus Olympio
hospitals.notes: Main public hospital and teaching hospital. French-speaking. Emergency department available but often overcrowded. Equipment limitations. Largest facility in the country.

hospitals.name: Clinique Biasa
hospitals.notes: Private clinic offering better care than public facilities. French-speaking. Cash payment typically required upfront.

hospitals.name: Polyclinique Internationale Saint-Joseph
hospitals.notes: Private facility with reasonable standards. French-speaking. Preferred by expatriates and international organizations.

dentalCare.availability: Very limited. A few dental clinics in Lomé. No dental services in rural areas.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care quality is basic. Sterilization standards may not meet international norms. Address all dental issues before traveling.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies, seek a private clinic in Lomé. Consider traveling to Accra, Ghana for better dental care if time allows.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated mental health crisis line available.
mentalHealth.internationalLine: Contact your embassy for referrals or use international telehealth services.
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Extremely limited. Most practitioners speak French only.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are very limited in Togo. Significant cultural stigma exists. CHU Sylvanus Olympio has a psychiatric department but resources are minimal. Telehealth with your home provider is the best option for ongoing support.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure is extremely limited throughout Togo.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Hospitals have minimal accessibility features. Wheelchair access is not standard.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Roads are often in poor condition. Motorcycle taxis (zémidjans) are the most common transport but not accessible.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Travelers with mobility challenges should plan very carefully. Hire local assistance. Most buildings, including hotels, lack elevators and ramps. Contact accommodations in advance.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.maskPolicy: No mandatory mask requirements. May be requested in healthcare facilities.
covidStatus.testing: Limited COVID testing available at CHU Sylvanus Olympio and some private labs in Lomé.
covidStatus.notes: Healthcare capacity for respiratory illness is very limited. Bring personal health supplies including masks and hand sanitizer.

insuranceClaimProcess: All facilities require upfront cash payment. Obtain detailed receipts and medical reports in French. Insurance claims are submitted after returning home. Keep all documentation and request translations if needed for your insurer.

commonCosts.currency: XOF (West African CFA Franc), prices shown in USD equivalent
commonCosts.note: Medical costs are very low by international standards but quality is correspondingly limited. Private clinics cost more but offer significantly better care.

medicalEvacuation.note: Accra, Ghana is the nearest city with better medical facilities (2-3 hours by road). For serious conditions, evacuation to South Africa or Europe may be needed. Ensure travel insurance covers evacuation from West Africa.
